pr.title: Do `check_coroutine_obligations` once per typeck root
pr.description:
We only need to do `check_coroutine_obligations` once per typeck root, especially since the new solver can't really (easily) associate which obligations correspond to which coroutines.

This requires us to move the checks for sized coroutine fields into `mir_coroutine_witnesses`, but that's fine imo.

r? lcnr
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.summary: Shifts coroutine obligation checking from once per coroutine to once per typeck root. Stalled coroutine predicates become a flat `FxIndexSet` on the typeck root, while `Sized` checks for coroutine fields are moved into `mir_coroutine_witnesses` (the coroutine layout path in the StateTransform implementation file). Regression tests split multiple coroutines into separate typeck roots and replace a crash test with a UI test for a coroutine inside an orphaned anon const.
analysis.originalLogic: Originally `check_coroutine_obligations` was called per coroutine def_id. It looked up `typeck.coroutine_stalled_predicates[&def_id]`, registered those predicates, and also registered `Sized` obligations for every entry of `coroutine.field_tys` when `unsized_locals` or `unsized_fn_params` was enabled. `coroutine_stalled_predicates` was a `LocalDefIdMap<Vec<(ty::Predicate<'tcx>, ObligationCause<'tcx>)>>` keyed by coroutine.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect per-coroutine transformation assumes each coroutine has its own retrievable stalled-predicate entry and that layout-dependent sized-field checks can be performed inside `check_coroutine_obligations`. With typeck-root-scoped obligations this fails because the new solver cannot easily associate obligations with individual coroutines, and an orphaned/nested coroutine may not have a direct typeck entry. A root-level-only change that merely aggregates predicates but leaves the `field_tys` sized checks in `check_coroutine_obligations` also cannot work, because root typeck has no per-coroutine layout. The corrected transformation stores all root predicates in one set and moves sized-field checks to `mir_coroutine_witnesses`, where `CoroutineLayout::field_tys` and the coroutine `LocalDefId` are available.
analysis.trigger: A typeck root contains one or more coroutines, especially multiple coroutines or a coroutine nested in an anonymous const/orphaned anon-const expression. Sized-coroutine-interior checking is additionally triggered only under `unsized_locals` or `unsized_fn_params`.
preconditions: `check_coroutine_obligations` receives the typeck root def_id, asserted by `debug_assert!(!tcx.is_typeck_child(def_id.to_def_id()));`
Stalled predicates are stored for the whole typeck root as `FxIndexSet<(ty::Predicate<'tcx>, ObligationCause<'tcx>)>` rather than keyed by coroutine def_id
`Sized` checks for coroutine fields run inside `mir_coroutine_witnesses`, after `compute_layout` and `check_suspend_tys`, where `coroutine_layout.field_tys` and the coroutine `def_id` are in scope
Field-sized checking early-returns unless `tcx.features().unsized_locals` or `tcx.features().unsized_fn_params` is enabled
Opaque type inference is bound to the typeck root via `with_opaque_type_inference(def_id)`
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source with `async`/generator coroutines, varying only in how many coroutines occur in each typeck root and whether a coroutine appears inside an anonymous const. The updated `clone-impl.rs` puts five coroutine scenarios into separate functions `test1()` through `test5()`, so each is its own typeck root. The new orphaned-anon-const test contains a coroutine in `{ async {} }` inside `Self::Assoc<{ async {} }>`. Field-sized coverage is relevant only with `#![feature(unsized_locals)]` or `unsized_fn_params`.
pitfalls: Do not keep keying stalled predicates by individual coroutine def_id after moving to per-typeck-root checking; the new solver cannot reliably associate obligations with specific coroutines.
Do not leave `Sized` coroutine-interior checks in the root-level `check_coroutine_obligations`; relocate them to `mir_coroutine_witnesses` where the per-coroutine layout exists.
Do not bind opaque type inference to a child coroutine's `typeck.hir_owner.def_id`; root-level checking must use the typeck root def_id.
Flattening the predicate map into a set changes ordering/deduplication behavior; the orphaned-anon-const regression expects duplicate E0220 diagnostics when `-Z deduplicate-diagnostics=no` is used.
Outer code that indexed `coroutine_stalled_predicates` by coroutine must be updated; the field is no longer a `LocalDefIdMap` of per-coroutine vectors.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI tests that exercise the changed granularity: put several coroutines in one typeck root, and separately place them in different roots, then verify every expected `Copy`/`Clone` trait-bound diagnostic still appears. Add or retain a coroutine nested inside an anonymous const to cover the orphaned-anon-const path and check for expected diagnostics rather than an ICE. For sized-field changes, enable `unsized_locals`/`unsized_fn_params` and verify `SizedCoroutineInterior` errors are still emitted from the layout/witness path. When splitting test functions, update expected stderr spans for shifted line numbers. This is source-level test strategy only; no compiler was built or run.
evidence: We only need to do `check_coroutine_obligations` once per typeck root, especially since the new solver can't really (easily) associate which obligations correspond to which coroutines.
This requires us to move the checks for sized coroutine fields into `mir_coroutine_witnesses`, but that's fine imo.
